panels.title: Audited now
Pipeline bottleneck — CPU against budget
panels.description: The single most useful panel here. cpu_self_cores is what this container actually burns; audit_permits is what the governor is willing to grant the backlog sweep. When CPU sits at the budget and permits fall toward 1, CPU is the binding constraint. When permits are high and in-flight is below them, the sweep is NOT taking what it was offered — that means it is blocked on something else (bytes, disk, or a barrier), and the bottleneck is downstream.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "server")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.stack == "kt-witness" and (r._field == "kt_witness_cpu_self_cores" or r._field == "kt_witness_cpu_machine_cores"))
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1m, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> keep(columns: ["_time","_field","_value"])

  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1m, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> keep(columns: ["_time","_field","_value"])

panels.title: Governor allowance actually taken
panels.description: in_flight divided by permits. At 1.0 the sweep is using everything the governor grants and more CPU would buy more throughput. Persistently below 1.0 means the CPU allowance is going unused and adding cores would buy nothing — look at bandwidth, the disk cache, or a barrier in the sweep instead.

  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, _value: if r.kt_witness_audit_permits > 0.0 then r.kt_witness_audit_in_flight / r.kt_witness_audit_permits else 0.0}))
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])

panels.title: Proof cache — the buffer between link and CPU
panels.description: The disk cache sits between downloading and verifying. FULL means downloads are outrunning verification, so bandwidth has headroom and CPU is the constraint. EMPTY while CPU is idle means the opposite: verification is starved and the link (or the CDN) is the constraint. This is the panel that tells the two apart.

  |> keep(columns: ["_time","_value"])

panels.title: Epochs verified per hour, by log
panels.description: Verification rate per log, at the resolution you are zoomed to. The counter is maxed within each window before differencing, so a machine joining or leaving the fleet shows as a step rather than being smeared across the window. Compare with 'by machine' below to see which box a change came from.

panels.title: Coverage integrity — holes in the swept range
panels.description: Epochs settled without being verified. These are gaps INSIDE the audited range, so they make the audited count overstate what was actually established. Retried on a growing backoff, so a value that keeps climbing means genuinely unfetchable proofs rather than a transient refusal. Non-zero here is why a log can be at B rather than B+.

from(bucket: "server")

  |> keep(columns: ["_time","origin","_value"])

panels.title: Largest unbroken verified run
panels.description: The honest form of the coverage claim. An audited COUNT says how much work was done and nothing about whether the result is a solid range or a sieve; only a solid range supports “this log's history is construction audited”. This line rising is real progress; the audited count rising while this stays flat is not.

panels.title: Logs — what the numbers do not say
Warnings and errors
panels.description:
Everything the witness logged above INFO. Normally empty, and that is the point: a withheld cosignature or a failed audit round appears here without anyone grepping a container that may since have been recreated.

`err` is structured metadata, so it is searchable — it used to render as `{}` in the events feed, which dropped the one field saying WHY a cosignature was withheld.

panels.title: Construction audits per hour, by log
panels.description:
Counted from `epoch verified` log lines, grouped by the `origin` structured metadata field. This is the view that makes a starved sweep obvious: when Proton's rebuild was holding sixteen cores, the AKD lines here thinned out while every counter still looked healthy.

`origin` is metadata rather than a label on purpose — it is absent from most lines, and a label present on only some lines of a stream splits the stream instead of grouping it.

panels.title: Proton replay — tip and history
panels.description:
Both retained trees report separately, because they make separate progress and reporting them as one hid exactly the case that occurred: the tip advancing while the history replay sat blocked behind it for hours, emitting nothing.

A replay waiting on the rebuild lock now says so before it takes the lock.

panels.title: Directory mutations worth a human
panels.description:
Removals, in-place overwrites and removals of labels the tree never held. None of these change the root, so a verifier that only compares tree hashes sees none of them — they are visible only by replaying the diff and reading what it did.

Removals alone are ordinary: Proton permits deletion within its retention window, and every removal observed so far has been explained by it. `overwritten` or `phantom` above zero is the reading that deserves attention.

panels.title: The fleet — who is verifying, and how much they can spare
Verification capacity offered, by machine
panels.description: Epochs each worker is currently willing to run at once, as the worker itself reports it — stacked, so the height is the fleet's total width. A line falling in the evening and rising overnight is the governor doing its job on somebody's laptop, not a fault. A line that stops is a worker that went away; a line at 1 is a machine that is busy with its owner's work and yielding, which is the intended behaviour and not a problem to fix.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "server")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.stack == "kt-witness" and r._field == "kt_witness_worker_parallel")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1m, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> group(columns: ["worker"])
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "worker"])

panels.title: Each machine against its own budget
panels.description: Measured load and self-imposed ceiling, in cores, as each worker measures its own host. Two machines will not agree on what a core is worth, so read each pair against itself rather than comparing across: load riding the budget is a worker using everything it is allowed, and load far above the budget is somebody else's work on that machine — which is exactly when the capacity above should be falling.

  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.stack == "kt-witness" and r._field == "kt_witness_worker_load_cores")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1m, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)

  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "worker"])

from(bucket: "server")

panels.title: Epochs verified per hour, by machine
panels.description: Who is actually doing the work, stacked — so the height is the fleet's total rate and each band is one machine. This is the panel that answers 'did adding that box help', which the by-log view cannot: there, four machines look like one fast witness, and a worker that quietly stopped looks like a log that got slower. witness-live follows the tip, witness-sweep walks history backwards, and the rest lease from the shared queue.

targets.query:
w = if int(v: v.windowPeriod) < 60000000000 then 1m else v.windowPeriod

from(bucket: "server")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.stack == "kt-witness" and r._field == "kt_witness_epochs_verified_by_worker_total")
  |> group(columns: ["worker"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: w, fn: max, createEmpty: false)
  |> derivative(unit: 1h, nonNegative: true)
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "worker"])
